title: Odysseus: Circe and the Sirens
subtitle: A year in an enchantress's bed, then ropes and beeswax

learningObjectives.text: How does Odysseus resist Circe's magic?
How does he hear the Sirens safely?

main.author: Homer
main.locator: Book 12, Circe’s instructions about the Sirens; local text file lines 5365-5370 (physical file lines, not ancient verse numbers)
main.excerpt: Therefore pass these Sirens by, and stop your men’s ears with wax that none of them may hear; but if you like you can listen yourself, for you may get the men to bind you as you stand upright on a cross piece half way up the mast,99 and they must lash the rope’s ends to the mast itself, that you may have the pleasure of listening. If you beg and pray the men to unloose you, then they must bind you faster.
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The men become swine
narrativeBlocks.body: On Circe's island, a scouting party finds an enchantress who turns guests into animals. They drink her potion and become pigs in a sty — men inside, beasts outside.

narrativeBlocks.title: The herb moly
narrativeBlocks.body: Hermes intercepts Odysseus on the path and gives him moly — a plant that neutralises her potion. When the magic fails and Circe reaches for him, Odysseus draws his sword; she yields, and restores his crew.

narrativeBlocks.title: A year gone like a summer
narrativeBlocks.body: Circe becomes his lover and host — and the crew stays a full year, feasting, while Ithaca waits. It is the men who finally remind him what he is for. Her parting gift is the road itself: you must first speak with the dead prophet Tiresias.

narrativeBlocks.title: Rope and beeswax
narrativeBlocks.body: Passing the Sirens — singers whose song wrecks every ship that listens — Odysseus wants to hear what no man has survived hearing. He plugs the crew's ears with wax, has himself lashed to the mast, and makes them swear: if he begs, bind him tighter.

narrativeBlocks.title: The original 'want to but shouldn't'
narrativeBlocks.body: The Sirens episode is the ancestor of every temptation scene: the only safe way to experience a fatal thing is to engineer your own helplessness in advance — a lesson in pre-commitment that economists still cite.

quiz.prompt: How does Odysseus resist Circe's transformation spell?

choices.text: Hermes gives him the herb moly, which neutralises her potion — then he draws his sword and she yields
He covers his eyes so her magic cannot reach him
He offers her his ship in exchange for his men
Athene strikes her wand from her hand

quiz.explanation: Moly protects him from the potion; once it fails, his drawn sword forces her to restore his crew.

quiz.prompt: How does Odysseus hear the Sirens and live?

choices.text: He plugs his crew's ears with wax and has himself tied to the mast, ordering them to bind him tighter if he begs
He steers wide around their island entirely
He drowns their song by shouting counter-verses
He sends a decoy sailor in his place

quiz.explanation: Pre-commitment: the crew cannot hear him or the song; his ropes hold even when he begs to be released.
